name.en: Fake parcel delivery text: “we couldn’t deliver your parcel”

how.en: A text or email says a courier such as Evri tried to deliver a parcel but couldn’t, for example because your address was incomplete. It asks you to follow a link within 24 hours to update your address or reschedule. The link leads to a fake site that asks for personal and payment details, or to a QR code that can install malware.

text.en: A text or email says it is from a delivery company.
It says a parcel couldn’t be delivered and you must act within 24 hours.
It gives a link to update your address or reschedule.
The site asks for your personal and card details.
Evri: Our driver attempted to deliver your parcel today but your address information is incomplete. Update your details within 24 hours: [link]
Royal Mail: Your parcel is being held at our depot. Reschedule your delivery here: [link]

en: A delivery message you weren’t expecting, with a link.
Being asked for card details or a fee to receive a parcel.
Don’t click the link. Track parcels only on the courier’s official website or app.
Forward the text free to 7726, and emails to the NCSC.
If you gave card details, call your bank straight away (you can dial 159).
